title: What looks like a cellphone in 1937 Mass. painting is again igniting time travel talk
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Off Beat Given that neither selfies or cellphones existed in 1937, conspiracy theorists went to the next obvious conclusion: Time travel must be real.

Smithsonian National Postal Museum A painting of the 17th century Massachusetts Bay Colony has gotten online attention once again, with both The Daily Mail and New York Post reporting on the bizarre conspiracy theory that the painting is proof time travel exists.

The painting, made in 1937, of Native Americans and English colonists in Springfield, has generated online buzz from internet conspiracy theorists who say one Native American man in the painting looks to be holding a cellphone.
